thread:
nora: Heads-up: saw a confusing error in the samplekit quickstart. When using function-calling + json_mode, our Python handler sometimes receives arguments as a quoted JSON string and crashes. New users hit this in the tutorial.

sam: Which SDK version and repro steps?

nora: py sdk 0.9.9 in the quickstart image. Steps: call the provided create_account function with json_mode=True and leave retry on. Occasionally the final message.function_call.arguments value is '"{\"email\":\"x@ex.com\"}"' instead of a dict.

mohit: That looks like a double-encode on the retry path. The stream coalescer used to json.dumps unconditionally in one code path. TS SDK auto-parses final strings; py didn't.

aya: Short-term doc patch: add a defensive snippet in the quickstart handler showing json.loads when args is a str. Also mention retry as the likely cause.

sam: Long-term: change the Python reassembler to try a single json.loads when final arguments is a string and only json.dumps when input is bytes. Add an interop test with the TS SDK to ensure parity across retry/no-retry.

ci-bot: Issue created #4555: "py-sdk: avoid double-encode for function_call.arguments on retry". Branch fix/fncall-retry-parse created and CI started.

mohit: I'll open the PR with the minimal patch + unit tests and add a changelog entry.

nora: Thanks; I'll update the samplekit notebook now with the workaround and a link to the issue so instructors can follow up. :thumbsup:
